primary.title: The Torah (The Pentateuch)
primary.author: Moses
primary.rationale: Traditionally attributed to Moses, this is the foundational text of Judaism and Christianity, containing laws, narratives, and genealogies. Its ancient origins make direct attribution challenging, but it is considered the primary source for understanding the figure of Moses.

secondary.title: Moses: A Life
secondary.author: Jonathan Kirsch
secondary.rationale: A comprehensive and accessible biography that examines Moses through historical, archaeological, and literary lenses, drawing on biblical texts and modern scholarship.

secondary.title: Moses: The Revelation of the Name
secondary.author: Joseph Blenkinsopp
secondary.rationale: This scholarly work by a renowned biblical scholar offers a critical examination of the figure of Moses, exploring his role in the formation of Israelite identity and religion.

secondary.title: Who is Moses? A Guide to the Essential Figure of the Bible
secondary.author: Richard Elliott Friedman
secondary.rationale: Friedman, a prominent biblical scholar, analyzes the historical and literary evidence for Moses, discussing different scholarly interpretations of his life and significance.

suggestions.notes: Primary sources directly authored by Moses are limited to the texts traditionally attributed to him, primarily the Torah. Historical and archaeological evidence for Moses as a specific individual is scarce, leading most scholarly research to focus on the textual and theological significance of the figure as presented in the Bible.
